---
title: "Running Benchmarks"
---

Every run is described by three words. A **suite** is a workload domain such
as `slm` or `vision`. A **workload** is one benchmark ID. A **profile** is the
run scale. That is the entire user-facing vocabulary.

## Profiles

| **Profile** | **Meaning** | **Use it for** |
|:---|:---|:---|
| `min` | Fast functional path | Install check, smoke test, classroom demo, CI |
| `max` | Candidate comparable scale | Validated assignments, artifact review, baseline candidates |
| `pro` | Research envelope with controlled variants and knobs | Architecture, backend, quantization, and serving studies |

`min` checks that a path runs, `max` exercises the candidate benchmark scale,
and `pro` opens the research space. Results from `min` are smoke signals, not
scores. A `max` result is comparable only when the workload quality contract,
release validation, and public asset policy all pass.

## Scenario Labels

The five score-bearing train-then-quality workloads use `training` as a
proposed MLPerf EDU scenario label. It is not an official MLPerf Inference
scenario and does not claim compatibility with an accepted MLPerf result
category. Performance-bearing inference rows retain the applicable
`single_stream`, `offline`, or `server` labels, subject to the independent
preview and candidate-status disclosures on this site.

## Selecting What Runs

A bare `--profile` selects that profile's default path. `--suite` narrows to
one domain, `--workload` selects one benchmark family, and `--variant` narrows
to a single variant within it.

```bash
uv run mlperf run --profile min                      # default min path, all suites
uv run mlperf run --suite vision --profile max       # one suite
uv run mlperf run --workload nanogpt-train --profile max
uv run mlperf run --workload smollm2-chat-inference --variant quantized-int8 \
    --profile max --model smollm2-135m
```

Add `--dry-run` to any of these to print the selection without running it.
Model-backed workloads accept `--model <alias>`; each benchmark page lists the
aliases its family supports.

## Fetch Before You Measure

```bash
uv run mlperf fetch --workload resnet18-train --profile max
uv run mlperf fetch --profile max --dry-run     # preview all downloads
```

`fetch` downloads supported datasets and model weights, verifies available
hash evidence, and populates the cache so the measured run contains no network
time. `uv run mlperf cache list` shows what is on disk.

## Reports and Output

Runs write JSON, HTML, and CSV reports plus a `.provd` provenance artifact.
Use `--output-dir` to choose the destination and `--open-report` to open the
HTML report on completion. Reports include hardware and software fingerprints,
dataset and model dossiers, and quality-target status; the
[results guide](results.qmd) covers how to read, verify, and package them.

## Power Telemetry

```bash
uv run mlperf run --workload dscnn-kws-train --profile max --power
```

`--power` adds aggregate estimated watts and joules to the report using
`powermetrics` on macOS or `nvidia-smi` on CUDA machines, without requiring
privileged hardware counters. Treat the numbers as coarse energy telemetry
for systems reasoning, not as calibrated power measurements.

## Reproducibility Basics

Runs declare seeds and deterministic dataset recipes where their registry
contracts require them. For candidate comparisons across machines, use
`--profile max`, publish the generated fingerprint block unmodified, and keep
the `.provd` artifact with the result. Score-bearing candidates must also pass
the quality target and evidence protocol declared on their benchmark page.
